question_record.context: A security incident involving a suspected identity theft (pass-the-ticket) originating from Julian Burke's account and device VNEVADO-Win10B was detected. The attacker used the stolen Kerberos ticket on the host VNEVADO-Win10V to access several resources. Later, a suspicious process stopping services was observed, indicating potential malicious activity related to data encryption or avoidance of detection.
question_record.question: What is the name of the known credential theft tool that was executed?
solution: An actor used Julian Burke (AadUserId '7fcf9695-68fc-4258-864d-e1e5b166c66f')'s Kerberos ticket from `VNEVADO-Win10B` to access resources on `VNEVADO-Win10V`.
A process with the filename `powershell.exe` suspiciously stopped services on the device likely to avoid detection or interfere with security operations.
A process with the filename `mimikatz.exe`, a known credential theft tool, was executed, indicating an attempt to dump users' credentials.

130.name: Suspected identity theft (pass-the-ticket)
130.description: An actor took Julian Burke (IT director)'s Kerberos ticket from VNEVADO-Win10B and used it on VNEVADO-Win10V to access 4 resources.

46.name: Suspicious process stopping services
46.description: A process suspiciously stopped services running on the device. An attacker might stop a service to avoid detection, removal of malware, and recovery. This is often done in conjunction with data encryption or destruction, to render the device unusable.

104.name: Malicious credential theft tool execution detected
104.description:
A known credential theft tool execution command line was detected.
Either the process itself or its command line indicated an intent to dump users' credentials, keys, plain-text passwords and more.
